articles.title: Two Ducks, But Record Still Broken! Tom Latham Surpasses Sehwag In Unwanted List
articles.description: New Zealand skipper Tom Latham endured a nightmare outing with the bat in the Wellington Test against India, registering two consecutive ducks to enter an unwanted chapter in Test cricket history. The left-handed opener failed to trouble the scorers in either innings, with Jasprit Bumrah proving to be his nemesis on both occasions. Latham's second-innings dismissal came on Day 4 when Bumrah got the better of him, with wicketkeeper Rishabh Pant completing the catch. The double failure has pushed the New Zealand captain past former India opener Virender Sehwag in an unwanted statistical race. Latham Moves Ahead Of Sehwag The latest dismissal took Latham's tally of Test ducks as an opening batsman to 16, taking him beyond Sehwag, who finished his Test career with 15 such dismissals. The New Zealand captain now holds the record for the highest number of ducks among Test opening batsmen. However, Latham still has some distance to cover before reaching the top of the overall list. Also Check || 'Kuch Ganda Sa Action...': Rishabh Pant Drags Jaiswal In Hilarious Stump-Mic Banter - WATCH West Indies opener Kraigg Brathwaite leads the unwanted chart with 19 ducks, while former England batsman Mike Atherton occupies second place with 18. Sri Lanka's Marvan Atapattu also features among the prominent names on this list, alongside Latham and Sehwag. India Hold Commanding Advantage Ahead Of Final Day Meanwhile, the contest remains tilted heavily in India's favour. New Zealand posted 368 in their first innings before India responded with a mammoth 720/9, eventually declaring their innings with a substantial 352-run advantage. The visitors began their second innings with a significant mountain to climb but struggled to build momentum against India's bowling attack. At stumps on Day 4, New Zealand had reached 119/2, leaving them trailing by 233 runs. With eight wickets still required, India will look to wrap up the contest on the final day and secure a crucial victory.

articles.title: WATCH: Pakistan Blind Cricketers' Plane-Crash Celebration Targets India After Controversial Win
articles.description: Celebrations by the Pakistan Blind Cricket Team have triggered fresh controversy after a video showed several players making gestures resembling fighter jets diving and crashing while posing with the trophy. The visuals have drawn comparisons with Pakistan pacer Haris Rauf's controversial actions during the 2025 Asia Cup, bringing the India-Pakistan rivalry back into focus. Pakistan Players Make Plane-Crash Gestures During Trophy Celebrations The video shows members of the Pakistan team celebrating with the trophy following their victory. However, some of the movements during the celebrations have attracted attention, particularly gestures that appear to imitate aircraft flying before plunging towards the ground. WATCH VIDEO One man wearing a black-and-white striped shirt is seen raising his right hand before bringing it sharply downwards at an angle. Another player, positioned towards the front of the group, stretches both arms out like wings and moves them from side to side, seemingly mimicking an aircraft in flight. Other members of the team also appear to participate in the celebrations. The gestures have prompted comparisons with an earlier incident involving the Pakistan men's cricket team during the Asia Cup. While the video has fuelled criticism, the players' precise intention behind the movements has not been independently established. Haris Rauf's Asia Cup Gesture Also Triggered Controversy The latest visuals have brought back memories of the India-Pakistan Super Four clash at the 2025 Asia Cup in Dubai on September 21. During that match, Pakistan fast bowler Haris Rauf was seen making a gesture that appeared to depict a fighter jet crashing. Rauf also displayed a '6-0' hand sign, which was widely interpreted as a reference to Pakistan's military claims about Indian fighter jets being shot down during the May 2025 conflict between the two countries. The gestures attracted considerable criticism and led to a formal complaint from the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) to the International Cricket Council (ICC), according to reports. The latest celebrations have therefore revived debate around the use of military references and aircraft-crash gestures in cricket-related events, particularly when India and Pakistan are involved. Pakistan's Trophy Win Also Faced Questions The celebrations have attracted further attention because of the circumstances surrounding Pakistan's reported victory. The match was called off without a ball being bowled, but the trophy was reportedly awarded to Pakistan on the basis of their superior net run rate. The decision did not go down well with the Indian team, which protested the outcome. The circumstances of the result added another layer to the controversy surrounding the celebrations. With the latest video circulating, the gestures have once again brought the sporting rivalry between India and Pakistan into the spotlight. The comparison with Rauf's Asia Cup actions has also ensured that the celebrations are being viewed in the context of the earlier controversy.
